## How to Convert Your SLSO Salary NSW: Hourly to Annual Pay

When you have an hourly rate for a School Learning Support Officer role in NSW, you want to know the annual equivalent, the fortnight, tax, and super. Use the formula: hourly × hours per week × 38 hours per week × 52 weeks. For a typical full-time 38-hour week, annual gross is hourly × 38 × 52. For example, a $30 per hour SLSO rate gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. Fortnightly pay is weekly × 2.

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, casual $33.05 per hour including 25% loading. The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage; award rates may be higher. For SLSO roles in NSW, the relevant award or enterprise agreement applies. The ABS average for NSW full-time ordinary time is $2108.8 per week (May 2026). This is an average, not this job's median. For SLSO salary NSW, your rate may be from an offer or current pay.

### Tax and Super on Your SLSO Salary

Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale: nil to $18,200; 15% to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above. Medicare levy 2%. Super guarantee 12% on ordinary earnings, paid on top, stops at $270,830 maximum contribution base. For SLSO salary NSW, super is on top of your ordinary earnings. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Important Notes

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, stops at $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, salary packaging not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For SLSO salary NSW, your hourly rate may be from an award or enterprise agreement. The National Minimum Wage is not a job median; it is an average.
